solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trouncing this country has given US airs!

indicators.note: a trouncing leaves US AIRS beaten out of shape, so their letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as printed

explanation.surface: A cold-war boast: beating this rival has made America insufferably smug.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals on US make it look like America; here it is just two letters of the fodder, and the exclamation mark hints at the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Russia is named only as 'this country', the nation the surface boasts of beating.

clue.text: Observe room on boat housing third of crew

indicators.note: 'third of crew' asks for the third letter of CREW
RM houses E, holding it inside

blocks.note: RM is the standard abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: A cabin on a vessel where one of the sailors bunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the room first with the boat after it; in a down clue it sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to observe, both in the sense of noticing and of commenting.

clue.text: Streaker grinned, upsetting small children

indicators.note: the letters of STREAKER GRINNED are upset, tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A naked runner smirks as a class of little ones is shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' reads as the streaker shocking the children; it is the instruction to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindergarteners are the youngest pupils, children at nursery or kindergarten.

clue.text: All wanting to consume bird’s breast

indicators.note: SUM wants to eat TERN, taking it inside

blocks.note: the sum is the whole, all of it

explanation.surface: Everyone is eager to eat the breast meat of the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird's breast' reads as one phrase; the 's is 'is', so the definition is 'breast' alone and the bird goes inside SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat bone at the front of the chest, so it names the breast by its skeleton.

clue.text: A male, in act, to stay young will adopt a female persona

indicators.note: A and M go in the act, DEED
NEVER AGE adopts A, taking it into itself

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
to never age is to stay young

explanation.surface: A man in a stage act keeps himself young by playing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edna Everage was the stage character of the Australian comedian Barry Humphries, a man in a wig and spectacles, so the surface describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edna was a female character played by a man, a persona rather than a person.

clue.text: Reviews just for the radio having little power in America

indicators.note: words 'for the radio' are heard, not read, so RIGHT is said and WRITE spelt
'in America' places the little P inside the letters for America, so US wraps round it

blocks.note: just means right, which sounds like write
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Critiques written only for broadcast, with little influence in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just for the radio' reads as 'only for radio'; 'just' is the word to be heard as RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Write-ups are reviews, as of a show or book in the press.

clue.text: Health-shop item Australian male found in can in Victoria

indicators.note: the Australian male is found in the can, inside TIN
the whole lot sits in Victoria, VIC

blocks.note: VIC is the abbreviation for the Australian state of Victoria
A is the abbreviation for Australian
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: An Aussie bloke in Melbourne buys a supplement sold in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: AM goes inside TIN to make TAMIN, and that goes inside VIC; 'Australian male' reads as one man, but it is two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin C tablets are a staple of health-food shops.

clue.text: Musician playing tune in record

indicators.note: playing the tune turns TUNE into a new arrangement
the rearranged tune goes in LIST

explanation.surface: A performer playing a melody as it is recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing tune' is what a musician does, so the surface hides that 'playing' works on the word TUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutenist is a musician who plays the lute.

clue.text: Skilful retuning of radio must take time

indicators.note: retuning the radio changes RADIO, putting its letters in a new order

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Tuning an old radio well is a skilled job that can't be rushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must take' simply adds T on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone clever with hands or mind is both adroit and skilful.

clue.text: Bloke backed chopping a tree

indicators.note: a bloke backed is MALE read from the back
chopping A cuts that letter out

explanation.surface: A man, with backing, takes an axe to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopping a tree' sounds like felling it; here 'chopping' removes the letter A from ELAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the elm is one broad-leaved species among the many that 'tree' covers.

clue.text: Key individual is seen west of European states

indicators.note: in an across clue west is to the left, so IS comes first

blocks.note: the Länder are the federal states of Germany and Austria

explanation.surface: An important person is spotted to the west of a group of European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key individual' reads as an important person; a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on a key, a small island, is an islander.

clue.text: Catch chap missing first penalty

indicators.note: GENT missing its first letter drops the G

blocks.note: to take the rap is to take the penalty

explanation.surface: A footballer is caught out after failing to take the opening penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing first penalty' reads as a football miss; 'missing first' belongs to 'chap'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to entrap someone is to catch them out, usually by trickery.

clue.text: Down-to-earth about spreading muck around soil — it accompanies many a scene

indicators.note: MUCK is spread out, its end CK moving round to the front of MU
the spread muck goes around GROUND
BASIC goes about the whole of it

explanation.surface: An earthy gardener spreads manure over the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading muck around soil' reads as gardening; the muck is split in two with its back end moved to the front, and 'down-to-earth' means plain, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Background music plays behind the action of many a film or stage scene.

clue.text: My fiddle part’s been cut

indicators.note: part of COOK has been cut away, its last letter

blocks.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them

explanation.surface: A violinist laments that some of their music has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My fiddle' reads as a violin; 'My' is an exclamation of surprise, and coo is its British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo! is a British exclamation of surprise, like My!

clue.text: After reforming, a clot is not easily moved

indicators.note: A CLOT IS is re-formed, its letters remade in a new shape

explanation.surface: Even when he mends his ways, a fool stays stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not easily moved' reads as physically stuck; it means emotionally unmoved.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stoical bears hardship without being moved to show feeling.

clue.text: Part of brain in this way split by a punch?

indicators.note: THUS is split open with A LAM put in the gap

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash; a lam is a blow

explanation.surface: A blow to the head can damage part of the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: LAM, to hit hard, is less familiar than the answer; the question mark flags the knockout scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalamus is a structure deep in the brain that relays signals.

clue.text: Provide clearer view of uranium in ailing pit

indicators.note: uranium goes in the ailing pit

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Inspecting the uranium in a failing mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old-fashioned form of illuminate, and the surface's mine hides it by suggesting lamps underground.
explanation.definitionFit: To illumine is to light up, giving a clearer view of something.

clue.text: Smuggled wine, showing rifle

blocks.note: to run goods is to smuggle them
sack is an old word for sherry-like white wine

explanation.surface: Contraband wine turns up with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' reads as a gun; it is the verb, to search and plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense of rifle, to search a place thoroughly and steal from it, is what ransacking a room means.

clue.text: ‘Ring’ specialist engrossed in opera literature

indicators.note: the answer is engrossed in the words, buried inside them

explanation.surface: A Wagner expert absorbed in writing about opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around 'Ring' point to Wagner's Ring cycle; the ring meant is the boxing ring, where Muhammad Ali was champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, world heavyweight champion, earned his fame in the boxing ring, so he is a specialist of that kind of ring.

clue.text: Pay-off from union demerger

blocks.note: the union is a marriage, so its demerger is a divorce
the money one former spouse pays the other

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union demerger' sounds like company finance or a trade union split; the union is a marriage, and its demerger is a divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimony is money paid to a former spouse after a divorce.

clue.text: Elvis noticeable in broadcast here?

indicators.note: broadcast scatters the letters of ELVIS NOTICEABLE

explanation.surface: Where might Elvis be seen on air?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Elvis shows up on screen when broadcast on cable television.
explanation.definitionFit: Cable television is a place where a broadcast of Elvis would be seen.

clue.text: Time out is upset, seat being jiggled

indicators.note: in a down clue IS upset is turned upside down, reading SI
the seat is jiggled, shaking its letters about

explanation.surface: A break is spoiled because the chair keeps wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time out is upset' reads as a disrupted break; 'upset' works on IS alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The afternoon rest taken in hot countries is a break from the working day, time out in the literal sense.

clue.text: Garage container one left about in the course of working

indicators.note: the letters come in the course of ON, between its O and N

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tin left lying about in a busy workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as lying around; it is CA, short for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the can with a long spout for lubricating engines is one container found in any garage.

clue.text: One in attendance when stuffing is knocked out of cricketer?

indicators.note: the stuffing is the middle, so the centre S is knocked out

blocks.note: in cricket the batsman is the player who bats

explanation.surface: A batsman is shaken after being bowled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock the stuffing out of' means to demoralise; here it takes out the middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman is an army officer's personal servant, one who attends on him.

clue.text: Defensive work to spoil archer’s options at first

indicators.note: 'options at first' asks for the first letter of OPTIONS

blocks.note: William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A fortification meant to limit an attacking bowman's choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer's options' reads as a bowman's choices; the 's only joins the archer to the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martello tower is a small round coastal fort, a defensive work.

clue.text: The writer turned round, identifying type of music

indicators.note: ME turned faces the other way, EM

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: An author spins round and names a genre of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned round' reads as one phrase; only 'turned' is the reversal, and 'round' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Emo is a style of emotional rock music.

clue.text: Artist that could be behind page in enthralling book?

definitions.text: that could be behind page in enthralling book?

blocks.note: a famous English painter of seascapes and sunsets

blocks.clueFragment: that could be behind page in enthralling book?
blocks.note: a gripping book is called a page-something; this word fills the gap behind 'page'

explanation.surface: A painter whose work is as gripping as a good novel.
explanation.walkthrough: An enthralling book is a page-turner, so TURNER comes after PAGE; J. M. W. Turner is the English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter J. M. W. Turner is an artist by example, and an enthralling book is a page-turner, where the word sits behind 'page'.

clue.text: Close to bar-room, receiving cold drink before going out?

indicators.note: the bar-room, TAP, receives C inside it

blocks.note: a tap or taproom is a bar
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Near the pub, having a cold one before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going out' reads as leaving the house; here it is going out like a light, falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a drink taken just before bed.
